assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine synthesis from a harsh, narrow problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) enabled huge scope and drives pharmaceutical process chemistry and materials; it is among the most used bond-forming methods in drug discovery. Chemically new: a general catalytic C(sp2)-N construction with a mechanistic picture (oxidative addition, amide binding, reductive elimination) that guided ligand evolution.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic variants and the key ligand classes from the mid-1990s onward, and both carried the field through decades of ligand and mechanism work. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precedent but not the general method; I am not certain of the finer details of the 1994-1995 priority exchange.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, enormous industrial use, stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue; the 2010 cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling and left C-N unrecognized.
uncertainties: Priority interplay between Kosugi, Buchwald and Hartwig in 1994-1995 is not something I can verify independently.
Committee may view it as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis made single-electron-transfer radical chemistry a mild, general tool for organic synthesis, opening bond constructions (including with Ni dual catalysis) that two-electron chemistry could not do; now ubiquitous in medicinal chemistry and late-stage functionalization. Clear, conceptually simple, and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: The 2008-2009 reports by Yoon, MacMillan and Stephenson are the usual landmarks; Nicewicz, Melchiorre, Konig and Fukuzumi also contributed importantly and the three-person limit forces exclusions. MacMillan already received the 2021 prize (organocatalysis), which complicates his inclusion; a trio without him is possible but uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen-plus years of rapid, independent adoption; mature in application though mechanistic details of some processes are still being refined. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Prior laureate status of MacMillan may argue for a different trio.
Credit is spread across many groups and priority is hard to rule on.
Ru/Ir photocatalysts have earlier inorganic photochemistry precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective catalytic C-H functionalization (directing groups, ligand-accelerated and template-controlled meta/remote activation) changes retrosynthetic logic and step economy, matching the efficiency theme in synthesis. Impact on late-stage diversification and total synthesis is clear and growing.
assessment.attribution: Yu pioneered ligand-enabled and template-controlled Pd(II) C-H activation, including remote selectivity; Sanford contributed Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis and oxidation and fluorination methods. Hartwig (borylation), Daugulis and Smith are also credible; the field is crowded, which makes a clean one-to-three configuration hard.
assessment.maturity: Strong adoption but the field is still moving; industrial manufacturing use is less established than for cross-coupling. Somewhat early relative to the top choices.
uncertainties: Dispersed credit across Yu, Sanford, Hartwig, Daugulis and earlier precedents.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable solid-phase oligonucleotide synthesis possible, underlying PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. Chemically elegant, robust, and used daily worldwide; its impact on molecular biology and medicine is vast.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and its automation (Beaucage's role in the original deoxynucleoside work is not in the supplied credit, as far as I recall); Hood is credited through instrumentation, a different kind of contribution. I propose Caruthers alone, accepting that allocation is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Decades of unchanged use; fully mature and arguably long overdue, though the long delay suggests the committee has repeatedly not selected it.
uncertainties: The exact share of credit for the chemistry versus the instrument is uncertain.
Prior prizes in nucleic-acid methods may weaken the novelty argument.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazol-2-ylidenes, phosphinocarbenes, cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) overturned the view that carbenes are only transient, and N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands (including in metathesis catalysts) and organocatalysts. Original, conceptually clear, broadly applied across synthesis and main-group chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand isolated the first stable (phosphino)carbene in 1988 and Arduengo the crystalline NHC in 1991; Nolan contributed Ru and Pd NHC catalysis, Rovis and Bode organocatalysis. Arduengo and Bertrand are the natural core; the others are applications.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed, with strong industrial use via NHC-metal catalysts.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed around fundamental isolation or catalysis, which changes the laureates.
Metathesis catalysts were recognized in 2005, partly overlapping applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues introduces a new modality in which small molecules recruit E3 ligases to eliminate proteins, with several clinical programs. A bold chemical concept, though more chemical biology and pharmacology than molecule-making; I would ask what is chemically new beyond the heterobifunctional design.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed the first PROTACs (2001); Ciulli did structure-guided VHL ligands and degrader design; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Credit across PROTAC versus molecular-glue discoveries is split, making the trio uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing: clinical validation is limited so far. Probably early.
uncertainties: Clinical approval has not yet confirmed the concept.
Attribution splits between PROTACs and glue degraders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert bases chemically without double-strand breaks, combining deaminase chemistry, protein engineering and CRISPR targeting, with therapeutic relevance. The chemical novelty is directed evolution of an adenine deaminase acting on DNA, which has no natural counterpart.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the intellectual leader; Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors on the CBE and ABE papers. Nishida and Kondo's independent cytidine deaminase editing work is a fair competing claim. Naming Liu with his two lead authors is plausible but uncertain, since committees usually credit senior investigators.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and first clinical results, but the 2020 CRISPR prize and the recent timeline make it comparatively early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize framing.
Role of trainees versus the senior investigator in credit.
Long-term clinical safety evidence is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered Lewis acid/base pairs can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, spawning metal-free hydrogenation and a new framework in main-group chemistry. Conceptually simple and original.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first reversible metal-free H2 activation in 2006 and developed the concept; Erker contributed pivotal complementary work (intramolecular systems, reactivity with alkenes and CO2). Both are appropriate, with Stephan the primary figure.
assessment.maturity: Roughly twenty years of confirmation, but practical and industrial uptake is limited compared with transition-metal catalysis; impact is more conceptual than methodological.
uncertainties: Scope and substrate generality remain modest versus metal catalysts.
